american-factory-2019.gazette: The Moraine plant had been a General Motors assembly line until it closed in 2008; Fuyao Glass America reopened the building in 2015 with Chinese management and local hires. Bognar and Reichert kept cameras on the floor through the safety complaints, the trip to Fuqing, and the union drive that followed. The vote went against the UAW.

apollo-11-2019.gazette: No narration, no interviews, no reenactments: every frame was shot in July 1969 and every voice comes from the mission's own recordings. Much of the material had gone unscreened for decades, including large-format reels held at the National Archives. The film's only editorial act is the cut.

honey-boy-2019.gazette: The script was written in court-ordered rehab in 2017, a therapeutic assignment turned into a screenplay about the years its author spent working as a child to keep a household running. LaBeouf then cast himself as his own father. Two other actors play him, at twelve and at twenty-two.
honey-boy-2019.prism: Playing your own father is one way to argue the man was more than his worst hours — and it quietly hands you final cut on someone who gets no rebuttal. The rehab exercise stayed an exercise; it just acquired a distributor.

house-of-hummingbird-2019.gazette: The camera stays back and scenes end without resolution — a slap, a diagnosis, a friendship dropped and never explained. Seoul in 1994 is building fast; in October the Seongsu Bridge comes down. Kim Bora shoots the household and the collapse at the same eye level.

i-m-no-longer-here-2019.gazette: Monterrey's Kolombia scene slowed Colombian cumbia to a crawl and danced to it in sculpted hair and oversized shirts, and the film keeps the records and the dialect intact. Frías cast from the same marginalized neighborhoods, at the point when cartel violence was pushing those young people out of them. Ulises ends up in Queens, where the haircut reads as nothing at all.

les-miserables-2019.gazette: Montfermeil is where Ly grew up and where he had a camera running during the 2005 riots; it is also the commune Hugo used, which is where the title comes from. The feature expanded a 2017 short shot on the same blocks, with the same estate and the same anti-crime unit. It took a share of the Jury Prize at Cannes that May.
les-miserables-2019.prism: Filming your own neighborhood buys accuracy and costs the exit — the people in the frame are the ones who live with how it plays afterward. Borrowing Hugo's title makes the harder claim: that the address has not moved in a hundred and fifty years.

once-upon-a-time-in-hollywood-2019.gazette: The summer of 1969 is assembled in detail — Spahn Ranch, the Cielo Drive address, the radio spots running between scenes — and then the recorded ending is refused. The Bruce Lee sequence drew objections from Lee's family on the same grounds: the film treats the record as material rather than as a limit. What it alters is legible only because everyone already knows what happened.

papicha-2019.gazette: Algiers in the 1990s turned a dress into a political object; during the Black Decade, unveiled and unaccompanied women were targets, and Meddour writes from the student years she lived there before her family left. The dormitory fashion show at the film's center sits directly on top of that documented campaign. Algeria pulled the scheduled 2019 release.

rocketman-2019.gazette: The Troubadour debut, the lyrics arriving from Taupin by post, the father who would not touch him, the stint in rehab — the beats are the documented ones. Fletcher stages them as production numbers, with the Troubadour crowd lifting off the floor. Elton John produced the film and approved the version in which he floats.
rocketman-2019.prism: A subject who produces his own biopic chooses which humiliations survive the edit, and fantasy is a useful solvent: it converts a claim into a feeling nobody can check. The levitation works precisely because the surrounding facts are verifiable — borrow enough record and the invention passes as memory.

so-long-my-son-2019.gazette: The one-child policy enters as a colleague enforcing it, and the late-1990s restructuring enters as an announcement read out on a factory floor. Wang Xiaoshuai runs one couple across three decades of both, jumping between them without warning. By the end the country has changed twice and the couple is still standing in the same year.

sorry-we-missed-you-2019.gazette: The driver is not employed. He is onboarded as a franchisee, buys his own van, and arranges his own cover when he cannot work — vocabulary Loach and Laverty collected from depots around Newcastle before writing. The handheld scanner does the managing.

the-farewell-2019.gazette: There was a diagnosis and there was a wedding, and only one of them was mentioned to the grandmother. Lulu Wang told the story on public radio before shooting it in Changchun, and the campaign ran it as 'based on an actual lie.' Her grandmother was still living when the film opened.
the-farewell-2019.prism: A deception built to shield one person becomes, on release, the thing everyone else is told — a gentle breach, but a breach. Wang keeps the lie and publishes it at the same time, and neither move cancels the other.

the-irishman-2019.gazette: Frank Sheeran's confession came late and on tape, and the investigators and reporters who worked the Hoffa case have never accepted it. Scorsese films the account as Sheeran gave it, down to the Detroit house and the afternoon of July 30, 1975. Hoffa's remains have never been found.

uncut-gems-2019.gazette: The plot runs on a series that actually happened — Boston against Philadelphia in the 2012 playoffs — with the broadcasts cut in as they aired. Kevin Garnett plays himself, and the bets track his real performances game by game. Every wager in the film is a wager on the past.

vitalina-varela-2019.gazette: Vitalina Varela reached Lisbon from Cape Verde three days after her husband's funeral, into a house he had lived in for decades without her. Costa filmed her playing herself in that neighborhood, shooting at night, in long takes, in the rooms themselves. Locarno gave the film its top prize and gave her the acting award.
vitalina-varela-2019.prism: Re-enacting your own widowhood is labor, and the trophy ends up honoring the performance rather than the loss it was cut from. She takes the credit and the prize; the house stays the house.
